title: The conormal module of an ideal generated by a regular sequence is free
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R$ a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and let $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. Then the $R/J$-module $J/J^2$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis the classes $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$; in particular $J/J^2\cong(R/J)^{\oplus c}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896), part (1): a regular sequence is quasi-regular (Definition 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, line 16878: the map R/J[X_1..X_c] -> (+)_n J^n/J^{n+1} of (equation-quasi-regular), line 16865, is an isomorphism), read in degree 1, where it is the map (R/J)^{(+)c} -> J/J^2, e_i -> f_i mod J^2; used as 'By Lemma 00LN we see that (J/J^2)_q is free of rank t' in the proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph

proof.text: *Notation and the claim proved by induction on $c$.* For a multi-index $I=(i_1,\dots,i_c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^c$ write $|I|=i_1+\dots+i_c$ and $f^I=f_1^{i_1}\cdots f_c^{i_c}$. Since $J$ is generated by $f_1,\dots,f_c$, the ideal $J^n$ is generated by the monomials $f^I$ with $|I|=n$, so every element of $J^{n+1}=J\cdot J^n$ has the form $\sum_{|I|=n}b_If^I$ with all $b_I\in J$. We prove, by induction on $c\ge0$, the claim $Q(c)$: *for every commutative ring $R$, every regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_c$ in $R$ with $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, every $n\ge0$ and every family $(a_I)_{|I|=n}$ of elements of $R$ with $\sum_{|I|=n}a_If^I\in J^{n+1}$, all $a_I$ lie in $J$* (this is the injectivity, in degree $n$, of the map $R/J[X_1,\dots,X_c]\to\bigoplus_nJ^n/J^{n+1}$, $X^I\mapsto f^I$, i.e. quasi-regularity, Definition 061P). Reduction: given such a relation, write $\sum_{|I|=n}a_If^I=\sum_{|I|=n}b_If^I$ with $b_I\in J$; then $\sum_{|I|=n}(a_I-b_I)f^I=0$, and $a_I\in J$ if and only if $a_I-b_I\in J$. So it suffices to prove $Q(c)$ for relations $\sum_{|I|=n}a_If^I=0$. For $c=0$ the only multi-index is $I=()$ with $|I|=0$, so only $n=0$ gives a nonempty family, and there the hypothesis $a_{()}\cdot1\in J^1=J$ is the conclusion; so $Q(0)$ holds. Let now $c\ge1$ and assume $Q(c-1)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896; proof lines 16909-16966), part (1), first paragraph (reduction to $\sum a_If^I=0$); the base case $c=0$ is not written in the source

proof.text: *The shorter sequence.* Put $J'=(f_1,\dots,f_{c-1})$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $f_1,\dots,f_{c-1}$ is a regular sequence in $R$: condition (1) for $i\le c-1$ is condition (1) for the given sequence, and $R/J'\neq0$ because $R/J'$ surjects onto $R/J\neq0$. Moreover condition (1) for $i=c$ says that $f_c$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/J'$; by induction on $m$ this gives: if $x\in R$ and $f_c^mx\in J'$ for some $m\ge0$, then $x\in J'$ (from $f_c\cdot(f_c^{m-1}x)\in J'$ get $f_c^{m-1}x\in J'$). Hence $Q(c-1)$ applies to $R$, the sequence $f_1,\dots,f_{c-1}$ and the ideal $J'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896; proof lines 16909-16966), part (1), second paragraph ('Because $f_c$ is not a zerodivisor on $R/J'$ (as $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a regular sequence)')

proof.text: *The inner induction.* Fix $n\ge0$. Primed multi-indices $I'=(i_1,\dots,i_{c-1})$ involve only $f_1,\dots,f_{c-1}$, so $f^{I'}\in J'^{|I'|}$. For $l\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ let $P(l)$ be the claim: *whenever $(a_{I',e})_{0\le e\le l,\ |I'|=n-e}$ are elements of $R$ with $\sum_{e=0}^l\bigl(\sum_{|I'|=n-e}a_{I',e}f^{I'}\bigr)f_c^e=0$, all $a_{I',e}$ lie in $J$.* We prove $P(l)$ by induction on $l$, both base and step by the following argument. Take such a relation. For $e\le l-1$ the term $\bigl(\sum_{|I'|=n-e}a_{I',e}f^{I'}\bigr)f_c^e$ lies in $J'^{\,n-e}\subseteq J'^{\,n-l+1}$ (as $n-e\ge n-l+1$), so the relation gives $\sum_{|I'|=n-l}(f_c^la_{I',l})f^{I'}\in J'^{\,n-l+1}$. By $Q(c-1)$ (step 2) in degree $n-l$, $f_c^la_{I',l}\in J'$ for every $I'$, and by step 2 again $a_{I',l}\in J'\subseteq J$. If $l=0$ these are all the coefficients and $P(0)$ is proved. If $l\ge1$, assume $P(l-1)$. Write $a_{I',l}=\sum_{k=1}^{c-1}g_{I',k}f_k$ with $g_{I',k}\in R$, and for $|K'|=n-l+1$ put $b_{K'}=\sum g_{I',k}$, the sum over the pairs $(I',k)$ with $|I'|=n-l$, $1\le k\le c-1$ and $I'+\varepsilon_k=K'$ ($\varepsilon_k$ the $k$-th unit multi-index), so that $f_kf^{I'}=f^{K'}$. Then $\bigl(\sum_{|I'|=n-l}a_{I',l}f^{I'}\bigr)f_c^l=\bigl(\sum_{|K'|=n-l+1}f_cb_{K'}f^{K'}\bigr)f_c^{l-1}$, and the relation becomes $\bigl(\sum_{|K'|=n-l+1}(a_{K',l-1}+f_cb_{K'})f^{K'}\bigr)f_c^{l-1}+\sum_{e=0}^{l-2}\bigl(\sum_{|I'|=n-e}a_{I',e}f^{I'}\bigr)f_c^e=0$, a relation of the form in $P(l-1)$. By $P(l-1)$, $a_{K',l-1}+f_cb_{K'}\in J$, hence $a_{K',l-1}\in J$ since $f_c\in J$, and $a_{I',e}\in J$ for $e\le l-2$. Together with $a_{I',l}\in J$ this proves $P(l)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896; proof lines 16909-16966), part (1), the induction on $l\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$

proof.text: *Conclusion of the induction on $c$.* Let $\sum_{|I|=n}a_If^I=0$ (step 1). Every multi-index of $c$ entries is $I=(I',e)$ with $I'$ primed, $e=i_c\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ and $|I'|=n-e$, and $f^I=f^{I'}f_c^e$. Putting $a_{I',e}=a_{(I',e)}$ the relation reads $\sum_{e=0}^n\bigl(\sum_{|I'|=n-e}a_{I',e}f^{I'}\bigr)f_c^e=0$, so $P(n)$ (step 3) gives $a_I\in J$ for all $I$. This proves $Q(c)$, and by induction $Q(c)$ holds for all $c$ (Lemma 00LN (1): a regular sequence is quasi-regular).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896; proof lines 16909-16966), part (1), the rewriting of $\sum a_If^I=0$ by powers of $f_c$

proof.text: *Degree $1$: the basis of $J/J^2$.* $J/J^2$ is an $R$-module killed by $J$, hence an $R/J$-module, with $\bar r\cdot(x\bmod J^2)=rx\bmod J^2$. Generation: every $x\in J$ is $\sum_ir_if_i$ with $r_i\in R$, so $x\bmod J^2=\sum_i\bar r_i\,(f_i\bmod J^2)$. Uniqueness: if $\sum_i\rho_i(f_i\bmod J^2)=\sum_i\sigma_i(f_i\bmod J^2)$ with $\rho_i,\sigma_i\in R/J$, choose lifts $r_i$ of $\rho_i-\sigma_i$; then $\sum_ir_if_i\in J^2$. The multi-indices with $|I|=1$ are the unit vectors $\varepsilon_i$, with $f^{\varepsilon_i}=f_i$, so $Q(c)$ with $n=1$ (step 4) gives $r_i\in J$, i.e. $\rho_i=\sigma_i$. So every element of $J/J^2$ is in exactly one way an $R/J$-linear combination of $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$: this family is a basis and $J/J^2$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $(\rho_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i\rho_i(f_i\bmod J^2)$ is an isomorphism $(R/J)^{\oplus c}\cong J/J^2$.
